style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The only psalm of David in the third book of the Psalter, and a prayer stitched almost entirely from older Scripture -- lines of Exodus, Deuteronomy, and other psalms woven into one continuous plea. It is titled simply 'A Prayer,' and it is built on the word 'for': bow Your ear, FOR I am poor and needy; guard my soul, FOR I am Your faithful one; be gracious, FOR I call all day; gladden my soul, FOR to You I lift it; FOR You, Lord, are good and forgiving. Fourteen petitions, and every one grounded in something about God or something about the pray-er's need. The center is a request no other psalm makes in these words: unite my heart to fear Your name -- one heart, undivided, instead of the scattered heart a hunted man lives with. The confession at the heart of the psalm is Sinai's: You, Lord, are a God full of compassion and grace, slow to anger, abundant in covenant love and faithfulness. The enemies arrive late and briefly; the last verse asks only for a sign of goodness that they will have to see. A servant's prayer, the son of a servant, asking the Master for what servants ask.

1.text: A prayer of David. Bend Your ear down, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and in need.
1.amp: A Prayer [tephillah] of David. Bow down [natah -- stretch, bend] Your ear [ozen], O LORD [YHWH], hear [anah -- answer] me: for I am poor [ani -- afflicted, humble] and needy [evyon].
1.notes: Titled simply tephillah (H8605), a prayer -- one of only five psalms so named. hatteh-YHWH oznekha (H5186, H241): bend Your ear -- the posture of Psalm 116:2 -- aneni (H6030), answer. And the first of the psalm's fourteen 'for's: ki-ani ve-evyon ani (H6041, H34) -- the plea's whole credential is need.

2.text: Guard my soul, for I am Yours in covenant loyalty; save Your servant who trusts in You, O my God.
2.amp: Preserve [shamar -- guard] my soul [nephesh]; for I am holy ['one whom thou favourest', chasid -- covenant-loyal, the KJV margin]: O You my God [Elohim], save [yasha] Your servant [ebed] that trusts [batach] in You.
2.notes: shomrah naphshi ki-chasid ani (H8104, H5315, H2623): not 'I am holy' in the sense of sinless but chasid -- one bound to God by chesed, and bound to be loyal in return; the margin's 'one whom thou favourest' catches it. hosha avdekha ha-boteach elekha (H3467, H5650, H982): save the servant who leans on You.

3.text: Be gracious to me, O Lord, for I keep calling to You all day long.
3.amp: Be merciful [chanan -- be gracious] unto me, O Lord [Adonai]: for I cry [qara] unto You daily ['all the day', yom, the KJV margin].
3.notes: chonneni Adonai (H2603, H136): grace from the Master -- Adonai appears seven times in this psalm, more than in any other. ki elekha eqra kol-ha-yom (H7121, H3117): the credential is persistence, the widow before the judge (cf. Luke 18:7).

4.text: Bring joy to the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
4.amp: Rejoice [samach -- gladden] the soul [nephesh] of Your servant [ebed]: for unto You, O Lord [Adonai], do I lift up [nasa] my soul.
4.notes: sammeach nephesh avdekha (H8055, H5315, H5650): make Your servant's soul glad -- joy asked for as a gift, not manufactured -- ki elekha Adonai naphshi essa (H136, H5375): Psalm 25:1's lifted soul, held up to be filled.

5.text: For You, O Lord, are good and ready to forgive, and rich in covenant love toward all who call on You.
5.amp: For You, Lord [Adonai], are good [tov], and ready to forgive [sallach -- forgiving by nature]; and plenteous [rav] in mercy [chesed -- covenant love] unto all them that call [qara] upon You.
5.notes: ki-attah Adonai tov ve-sallach (H136, H2896, H5546): sallach is an adjective found only here in the Bible -- forgiving as a standing disposition, not an occasional act. ve-rav-chesed le-khol-qoreekha (H7227, H2617, H7121): abundant covenant love to ALL who call -- the door has no list.

6.text: Give ear, O LORD, to my prayer; pay attention to the sound of my pleas for grace.
6.amp: Give ear [azan], O LORD [YHWH], unto my prayer [tephillah]; and attend [qashab -- listen intently] to the voice [qol] of my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace].
6.notes: haazinah YHWH tephillati (H238, H8605): the psalm's title-word again -- ve-haqshivah be-qol tachanunotai (H7181, H6963, H8469): attend to the sound of my grace-pleas. The second round of petitions begins, mirroring verse 1.

7.text: On the day of my trouble I will call on You, for You will answer me.
7.amp: In the day [yom] of my trouble [tsarah] I will call [qara] upon You: for You will answer [anah] me.
7.notes: be-yom tsarati eqraekka (H3117, H6869, H7121): the day of trouble is when the calling happens -- and the 'for' this time is confidence, not need: ki taaneni (H6030), because You WILL answer. Psalm 50:15's promise turned into a plan.

8.text: There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours.
8.amp: Among the gods [elohim] there is none like unto You, O Lord [Adonai]; neither are there any works like unto Your works [maaseh].
8.notes: en-kamokha ba-elohim Adonai (H430, H136): Exodus 15:11's 'who is like You among the gods?' answered flatly -- no one. ve-en ke-maasekha (H4639): and no deeds like Yours. The psalm shifts from asking to confessing; the middle section (vv. 8-13) is what the servant knows about his Master.

9.text: All the nations You have made will come and bow down before You, O Lord, and they will glorify Your name.
9.amp: All nations [goy] whom You have made [asah] shall come [bo] and worship [shachah -- bow low] before [panim] You, O Lord [Adonai]; and shall glorify [kabad] Your name [shem].
9.notes: kol-goyim asher asita (H1471, H6213): every nation is His by manufacture -- yavou ve-yishtachavu le-phanekha (H935, H7812, H6440): they will come and bow. The vision of Psalm 22:27 and Revelation 15:4 (which quotes this verse): the nations' worship is not a hope but a schedule.

10.text: For You are great and do wonders; You are God -- You alone.
10.amp: For You are great [gadol], and do [asah] wondrous things [pala -- wonders beyond human ability]: You are God [Elohim] alone.
10.notes: ki-gadol attah ve-oseh niphlaot (H1419, H6213, H6381): greatness proved by wonders -- attah Elohim le-vaddekha (H430): You are God, You ALONE. The Shema's monotheism in a prayer: the reason the nations will come (v. 9) is that there is no one else to go to.

11.text: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and I will walk in Your truth; make my heart one, to fear Your name.
11.amp: Teach [yarah -- instruct, point the way] me Your way [derek], O LORD [YHWH]; I will walk [halak] in Your truth [emeth]: unite [yachad -- make one, join together] my heart [lebab] to fear [yare] Your name [shem].
11.notes: horeni YHWH darkekha (H3384, H1870): teach me Your road -- Psalm 25:4's request -- ahallekh ba-amittekha (H1980, H571). Then the petition no other psalm makes in these words: yached lebabi le-yirah shemekha (H3161, H3824, H3372, H8034) -- UNITE my heart, make it one thing, to fear Your name. A hunted man's heart is scattered in a dozen directions; he asks for a single one (cf. James 1:8; Jeremiah 32:39).

12.text: I will give You thanks, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify Your name forever.
12.amp: I will praise [yadah] You, O Lord [Adonai] my God [Elohim], with all my heart [lebab]: and I will glorify [kabad] Your name [shem] for evermore [olam].
12.notes: odekha Adonai Elohai be-khol-lebabi (H3034, H136, H430, H3824): the united heart of verse 11 now put to use -- ALL of it, thanking. va-akhabbedah shimkha le-olam (H3513, H8034, H5769): the nations will glorify the Name (v. 9); the servant starts now.

13.text: For Your covenant love toward me is great; You have rescued my soul from the deepest Sheol.
13.amp: For great [gadol] is Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love] toward me: and You have delivered [natsal] my soul [nephesh] from the lowest [tachti -- the depths] hell ['grave', sheol, the KJV margin].
13.notes: ki-chasdekha gadol alai (H2617, H1419): covenant love great UPON me -- the gadol of verse 10 brought down to one life. ve-hitsalta naphshi mi-sheol tachtiyyah (H5337, H5315, H7585, H8482): from Sheol's bottom floor -- the deepest grave, a death David had been close enough to describe.

14.text: O God, arrogant men have risen up against me, and a mob of ruthless men has hunted for my life -- men who do not keep You in view.
14.amp: O God [Elohim], the proud [zed -- the insolent] are risen [qum] against me, and the assemblies [edah] of violent ['terrible', arits -- ruthless, the KJV margin] men have sought [baqash] after my soul [nephesh]; and have not set [sum] You before them.
14.notes: zedim qamu-alai (H2086, H6965): the insolent risen up -- va-adat aritsim biqshu naphshi (H5712, H6184, H1245, H5315): a congregation of the ruthless hunting his life. The diagnosis is theological: ve-lo samukha le-negdam (H7760) -- they have not set You in front of them. Violence begins with a God kept out of view.

15.text: But You, O Lord, are a God full of compassion and grace, slow to anger and abundant in covenant love and faithfulness.
15.amp: But You, O Lord [Adonai], are a God [El] full of compassion [rachum], and gracious [channun], longsuffering [erek aph -- slow to anger], and plenteous [rav] in mercy [chesed -- covenant love] and truth [emeth].
15.notes: ve-attah Adonai -- the 'but You' pivot -- El rachum ve-channun, erekh appayim ve-rav-chesed ve-emet (H410, H7349, H2587, H750, H639, H7227, H2617, H571): Exodus 34:6 quoted whole, the sentence God spoke about Himself on Sinai and Israel could not stop repeating. Against the ruthless, David sets the Name's own self-description.

16.text: Turn toward me and show me grace; grant Your servant Your strength, and save the son of Your maidservant.
16.amp: O turn [panah] unto me, and have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon me; give [natan] Your strength [oz] unto Your servant [ebed], and save [yasha] the son [ben] of Your handmaid [amah].
16.notes: peneh elai ve-chonneni (H6437, H2603): turn Your face and be gracious -- tenah-uzzekha le-avdekha (H5414, H5797, H5650): give YOUR strength to Your servant; ve-hoshiah le-ben-amatekha (H3467, H1121, H519): the son of Your handmaid -- a house-born servant, belonging by birth (cf. Psalm 116:16). The plea of one who has no claim but membership.

17.text: Work a sign of goodness for me, so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame -- because You, O LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
17.amp: Show [asah -- work, make] me a token [ot -- sign] for good [tov]; that they which hate [sane] me may see [raah] it, and be ashamed [bosh]: because You, LORD [YHWH], have holpen [azar] me, and comforted [nacham] me.
17.notes: aseh-immi ot le-tovah (H6213, H226, H2896): make with me a sign for good -- something visible, so that the haters (sone'ai, H8130) raah and bosh (H7200, H954). The psalm ends in the perfect tense: ki-attah YHWH azartani ve-nichamtani (H5826, H5162) -- You HAVE helped, You HAVE comforted. Fourteen petitions, and the last word is a thank-you already.
